$comment: JURISDICTIONAL SUBJECTS — which state a rule is asking about.
D4.11 found the same question answered four ways across the codebase, two of them
opposite: the stamp author read operating_state first because stamp duty follows where
the instrument is executed and the property sits; the governing-law author read
governing_law_state first for the opposite and equally correct reason. Four authors each
reached for the right subject, had no vocabulary to name it, and encoded their intent as a
`operating_state` is SYNTACTICALLY typed and SEMANTICALLY untyped: it has a value domain
and no contract saying which subject it represents. This file gives the subjects names so
a rule can say which one it means instead of guessing through a chain.
THE GROWTH RULE. A subject becomes REPRESENTABLE when an authored rule actually needs it —
never before. Adding six intake questions to serve rules nobody has written would be the
intake equivalent of a premature abstraction, and this repository already carries 148 dead
questions from the last time that happened. A subject with `fact: null` is declared and
deliberately unresolvable: a rule naming it fails loudly rather than falling back to a
NOTHING HERE ADDS AN INTAKE QUESTION. PROPERTY_SITUS resolves to `operating_state` because
for the property families that is already what the field means — the repair makes an
existing implicit meaning explicit rather than asking the user anything new.

subjects.subject: CHOSEN_GOVERNING_LAW
subjects.statement: The law the parties selected to govern the agreement.
subjects.note: A party choice. Correct for contractual questions and wrong for anything that follows the situs of immovable property, which the parties cannot choose.

subjects.subject: PROPERTY_SITUS
subjects.statement: The state in which the immovable property is situated.
subjects.note: Stamp duty, registration and rent control follow the situs regardless of the parties' choice of law. `operating_state` is used because in the property families it already carries this meaning — see documentHardening.js:2608, which reads it first for exactly this reason. If a family is ever authored where operating_state means something else, this mapping must become per-family rather than portfolio-wide.

subjects.subject: WORKPLACE_LOCATION
subjects.statement: The state in which the work is performed.
subjects.unrepresentable: No typed fact carries it. `work_location` is free text in 3 families and holds an address, not a state. Shops and Establishments legislation, professional tax and several labour thresholds are state-specific and would need this.

subjects.subject: PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE
subjects.statement: The state in which the contractual obligation is to be performed.
subjects.unrepresentable: `delivery_location` is free text in 3 families and holds an address.

subjects.subject: PARTY_ESTABLISHMENT
subjects.statement: The state in which a party is resident or established.
subjects.unrepresentable: Party addresses are free text in 26 families. Extracting a state from them is possible and would carry an INFERRED provenance, which is a different question from whether the fact exists.

subjects.subject: FORUM
subjects.statement: The place whose courts or tribunals the parties have submitted to.
subjects.unrepresentable: `execution_city` and `arbitration_city` are free text and hold cities, not states. A forum is also often a city rather than a state, so this subject may need a different value domain entirely.
